item.title: India’s ‘Clean Lake’ Hero Lies Forgotten After Accident, Facing Amputation | FairPlanet
item.description: Once hailed as India’s “Swachh Bharat Ambassador” for cleaning the polluted waters of Wular Lake, Kashmiri boy, Bilal Ahmad Dar is now trapped in a tin-shed room, bedridden and battling the threat of amputation after a brutal road accident. The awards that once made him a national symbol of hope now hang like silent reminders of a life the world has moved on from. As medical bills soar beyond ₹14 lakh (€15,500), Bilal waits, not for applause, but for someone to help him stand again.

item.title: Indian Farmers oppose India–US Trade Deal, fear loss of livelihoods in the Himalayan states | FairPlanet
item.description: Millions of Indian farmers protested a proposed India–US interim trade agreement on 12 February across India, fearing that limited agricultural concessions could expose small-scale growers to subsidised imports. In India’s Himalayan regions, apple farmers warn that such competition could deepen climate-driven vulnerabilities, threatening not only rural livelihoods but also fragile mountain ecosystems already under stress.

item.title: Kibera – What the State Withholds, the Community Builds | FairPlanet
item.description: Denied water, security, and legal recognition for over a hundred years, the people of Kibera have built their own system of survival. From new water infrastructure to community-based protection mechanisms, local actors have stepped in where the state remains absent. Yet these solutions, while effective, expose both the ingenuity of the community and the limits of resilience in the face of structural neglect.

item.title: Cameroonians Transform Plastic Waste into Sustainable Roofing Tiles | FairPlanet
item.description: In Cameroon, plastic pollution remains a major environmental and health challenge, worsened by widespread burning and inadequate waste management. Through the local initiative AMABO Tiles, Cameroonians transform discarded plastics into sustainable roofing tiles, providing construction materials while reducing reliance on energy-intensive cooling. This innovation demonstrates how community-led recycling solutions can address environmental, social, and economic issues simultaneously.

item.title: War-Affected Sudanese Students Stranded as UK Halts Study Visas | FairPlanet
item.description: A new UK migration policy introduced in March has restricted study visas for Sudanese nationals, prompting British universities and scholarship bodies to withdraw admission offers and funding considerations. For students already displaced by war, studying in the UK provided a viable pathway to rebuilding their lives. Experts and advocates argue the restrictions conflate asylum with student migration, penalising war-affected civilians for a broader political agenda.
